title: Six writing rules collapse into unplaceable-reference
summary: This change retires six writing-lint rule ids — bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name and undefined-name-at-start — and folds all of them into the single existing rule unplaceable-reference. The rule now also carries the old link warning: a labelled repo reference with no Markdown link is placed but still warns. Because the old ids are gone, every place a user could still name one — a suppression marker, a writing.levels override, an osf-expect declaration, osf explain, or the OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS environment variable — now reports an error or notice that names unplaceable-reference instead of failing silently. The config key writing.chat_local_labels is removed outright, and the stop hook loads config through a new path that keeps the retired-variable notice out of the text an agent reads as its next instruction.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: main.rs
nodes.summary: Dispatches every subcommand. explain now short-circuits a retired rule id and points at its replacement instead of printing 'no such rule'.

nodes.label: osf lint writing
nodes.summary: The command a person runs. It loads config with the retired-variable notice enabled, so a stale OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS is announced on stderr.

nodes.label: osf hook stop
nodes.summary: The agent-facing refusal path. It now loads config through load_for_hook, which suppresses the retired-variable notice so it never lands in the text an agent reads as its next instruction.

nodes.label: osf verify
nodes.summary: Pre-commit and pre-push checks. Its declared-fixture check now passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS and emits expectation-retired-rule findings.

nodes.label: config::load
nodes.subtitle: load_announcing(.., announce_retired)
nodes.summary: The single loader behind both entry points. It applies env, then rejects a writing.levels key naming a retired rule and rewrites the unknown-key error for writing.chat_local_labels.

nodes.label: config::load_for_hook
nodes.summary: New thin wrapper: no flags, no gate, and announce_retired false, so a hook's stderr stays clean of migration notices.

nodes.label: retired_env_notices
nodes.summary: Builds one notice line per retired environment variable that is set, naming the replacements. Called only when announce_retired is true.

nodes.label: reject_retired_levels
nodes.summary: Turns a writing.levels entry keyed by any retired rule id into a hard config error naming unplaceable-reference, rather than a silent no-op.

nodes.label: WritingConfig
nodes.subtitle: chat_local_labels removed
nodes.summary: The chat_local_labels field and its default list are gone; the env field mapping for OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS is gone with it.

nodes.label: RETIRED_RULE_IDS
nodes.subtitle: 6 old ids -> unplaceable-reference
nodes.summary: The single table every migration path reads: suppression validation, level overrides, expectation checks and osf explain all consult it.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.summary: No longer calls undefined_names; runs unplaceable_reference and passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS into apply_suppressions. apply_context now resolves every rule from its own evidence, with no special case for unplaceable-reference.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference
nodes.summary: The surviving rule. It now emits a warning for a labelled repo reference with no link, via the new unlinked_finding helper, absorbing the retired reference-without-link behaviour.

nodes.label: unlinked_finding
nodes.summary: Returns a warning-level unplaceable-reference finding when a repo-qualified number is placed but not wrapped in a Markdown link.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.summary: Six rule_meta entries are deleted; the unplaceable-reference entry gains a sentence about the unlinked-reference warning.

nodes.label: apply_suppressions
nodes.summary: Takes a retired_rules slice and threads it into validate_ids, so a suppression naming a retired id still errors but the message names the replacement.

nodes.label: validate_ids
nodes.summary: Looks an unknown id up in the retired table and rewrites the diagnostic to say the rule was replaced, instead of a bare 'not a rule id'.

nodes.label: expectation::check
nodes.summary: Gains a retired_rules parameter and a retired field on Mismatch. A declared retired id is reported on its own, and its replacement firing is not also reported as unexpected.

nodes.label: expectation_findings
nodes.summary: Renders each retired declaration as an expectation-retired-rule error naming the replacement, chained after missing and unexpected.

nodes.label: writing fixtures
nodes.summary: The chat-local-named-label pair is deleted, a new unlinked-reference fixture is added, and the remaining fixtures drop their now-retired osf-expect ids.

edges.label: load / load_for_hook
edges.summary: Both entry points reach the same loader; only the announce_retired flag differs.

edges.label: no retired notice
edges.summary: The hook path deliberately takes the quiet loader so migration chatter never reaches an agent's next instruction.
The person-facing path takes the announcing loader.
Runs after the layered config is finished, before the result is returned.
Produces the resolved WritingConfig, now without chat_local_labels.

edges.label: placed but unlinked
edges.summary: The absorbed behaviour: a labelled repo reference with no link warns instead of passing silently.

edges.label: RETIRED_RULE_IDS
edges.summary: Suppression validation now knows which ids are retired.
Threads the retired table into per-marker id validation.
Declared fixtures are checked with the retired table.
osf explain consults the table before reporting 'no such rule'.
Level and remediation are resolved from the surviving metadata.
Fixtures declare the ids the lint now produces.

flows.title: A retired rule id is named, and the tool answers with its replacement
flows.summary: Four entry points where a user can still write one of the six retired ids, and what each now says instead of failing silently.

messages.label: writing.levels names a retired id
messages.note: reject_retired_levels returns an error naming unplaceable-reference instead of letting the level silently do nothing.

messages.label: marker names bare-reference
messages.note: Still an error, but the message says it was replaced by unplaceable-reference.

messages.label: Mismatch.retired
messages.note: A retired declaration is reported on its own; its replacement firing is not also flagged unexpected.
